formal_statement: have x1 : List (ℕ × ℕ) := [((0 : ℕ), (7 : ℕ)), ((0 : ℕ), (8 : ℕ)), ((0 : ℕ), (10 : ℕ)), ((1 : ℕ), (7 : ℕ)), ((1 : ℕ), (9 : ℕ)), ((1 : ℕ), (13 : ℕ)), ((2 : ℕ), (8 : ℕ)), ((2 : ℕ), (12 : ℕ)), ((2 : ℕ), (13 : ℕ)), ((3 : ℕ), (7 : ℕ)), ((3 : ℕ), (11 : ℕ)), ((3 : ℕ), (12 : ℕ)), ((4 : ℕ), (10 : ℕ)), ((4 : ℕ), (11 : ℕ)), ((4 : ℕ), (13 : ℕ)), ((5 : ℕ), (9 : ℕ)), ((5 : ℕ), (10 : ℕ)), ((5 : ℕ), (12 : ℕ)), ((6 : ℕ), (8 : ℕ)), ((6 : ℕ), (9 : ℕ)), ((6 : ℕ), (11 : ℕ))]; have x2 : (Fin (14 : ℕ) → Bool) → Prop := fun (x2 : Fin (14 : ℕ) → Bool) => ∃ (x3 : Fin (14 : ℕ)) (x4 : Fin (14 : ℕ)), (↑x3, ↑x4) ∈ x1 ∧ x2 x3 = Bool.true ∧ x2 x4 = Bool.true; have x3 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit → Fin (14 : ℕ) → Prop := fun (x3 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (x4 : Fin (14 : ℕ)) => ∀ (x5 : Fin (14 : ℕ) → Bool), x3.eval (List.ofFn x5 ++ [PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or.eval [x5 (0 : Fin (14 : ℕ)), x5 x4]]) = Bool.true ↔ x2 x5; ∀ (x4 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (x5 : List PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) (x6 x7 : ℕ), x4.gates = { op := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.GateOp.or, inputs := [x6, x7] : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate } :: x5 → x6 < (14 : ℕ) → x7 < (14 : ℕ) → x6 ≠ x7 → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 x4 → (∀ (x13 : Fin (14 : ℕ) → Bool), x4.eval (List.ofFn x13) = Bool.true ↔ x2 x13) → ∃ (x14 : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 x14 ∧ x14.size + (1 : ℕ) ≤ x4.size ∧ (x3 x14 (1 : Fin (14 : ℕ)) ∨ x3 x14 (7 : Fin (14 : ℕ)) ∨ x3 x14 (9 : Fin (14 : ℕ)))
plain_statement: The edge function of the Heawood graph (14 inputs, 21 edges). A circuit of AND and OR gates, at most two inputs a gate, for it whose first gate is the OR of two different inputs gives a circuit of that kind, one gate smaller, that computes the function when also given the wire OR(x_0, x_1), OR(x_0, x_7) or OR(x_0, x_9).
title: A step toward: A step toward: Every circuit of AND and OR gates for the edge function of the Heawood graph has at least 27 gates
